name: SCAI The Bathhouse
about_text: SCAI The Bathhouse is a contemporary art gallery in Yanaka, Tokyo, housed in a converted 200-year-old public bathhouse near Ueno's museum district. Established in 1993 (the gallery also cites 1989 elsewhere), it has built the careers of major postwar Japanese artists associated with the Mono-ha movement, as well as figures such as Toshikatsu Endo and Mariko Mori, while promoting younger talents like Kohei Nawa and Reijiro Wada. International artists including Anish Kapoor, Darren Almond, Apichatpong Weerasethakul, and He Xiangyu have created works in dialogue with Japanese culture through the gallery. SCAI has also organized public art projects in Tokyo, including installations at Roppongi Hills, and operates additional spaces—SCAI PARK in Tennozu Isle and SCAI PIRAMIDE in Roppongi—extending its program of exhibitions, preservation, and experimental projects for emerging artists.
